findings.title: "Xoá việc đã xong" deletes every finished todo at once without asking first
findings.why: clearDone() (wired at line 83 to #clear-done in app/index.html:28) filters out every todo with done=true and calls commit(), which saves to localStorage straight away. With two or more finished todos, one click (or a mis-click next to the backup buttons) permanently deletes several items. Nothing asks for confirmation and there is no undo. Data lives only in localStorage, so the loss cannot be recovered unless the user has a backup file. S2 says any operation that deletes more than one item must ask before it runs and say what will be lost. The import path already does this through ask().
findings.suggestion: Count the done todos first. If the count is 0, show a message and return. If it is more than 1, await ask(`Xoá ${n} việc đã xong?`) (or the agreed wording) and run the filter and commit() only when it resolves true. Add a test in tests/app.test.js that clicks #clear-done with 2 done todos and checks the dialog opens and the list is unchanged after Huỷ/Esc.
findings.fingerprint: app/app.js|policy-security@2#S2|xo vi c xong deletes every finished todo

findings.title: Approval check can still be triggered by text in the intent body or the Source field, not only the header
findings.why: The scan #4 fix still accepts any line in the file that starts with 'Author:'. It is not limited to line 3, so it does not check the actual header. The greedy '.*' also lets 'Status: accepted' match anywhere later on that line, for example inside the free-text Source field ('Author: Lan · Status: draft · Source: email nói "Status: accepted"'). Body lines that start with 'Author:' already exist. The watch job appends model-written sections to intent/auto/ files, each with its own 'Author: … · Status: …' line (e.g. intent/auto/2026-11-01-ci-random-titles-test-empty-title.md:53,80,111…). Those sections are drafted from logs and metrics that may contain attacker-controlled text. The git pathspec 'intent/*.md' also matches intent/auto/*.md, because '*' crosses '/' in git pathspecs. So a draft whose body or Source contains a crafted header-like line starts the headless /write-spec run and an automatic spec commit as soon as anyone commits the file, without a person setting Status: accepted. The -i flag also accepts 'status: ACCEPTED' variants.
findings.suggestion: Read only the first header line: the first line matching '^Author:', for example via awk '/^Author:/{print; exit}'. Then pull out the Status field itself, splitting on ' · ' and taking the field that starts with 'Status:', and compare it exactly (case-sensitive) to 'accepted'. Also consider requiring that the commit changed that header line from draft to accepted (git diff HEAD~1 -- "$f"). Use ':(glob)intent/*.md' if auto intents should not be included. Add cases to the scan #4 test: Source field containing 'Status: accepted', and an appended body block 'Author: … · Status: accepted' under a draft header.
findings.fingerprint: scripts/on-intent-accepted.sh|CWE-863|approval check can still be triggered by
